title: Enabling statutes and the source of agency power
shortTitle: Enabling statutes and the source of agency power
summary: An enabling statute is legislation that creates or authorizes an agency’s powers, purposes, and jurisdiction.
notes:
An agency must identify statutory authority for the action it takes. Congress may specify exact factual triggers and outcomes, or permit judgment under broader standards. The statute supplies both an operational instruction and a claimed source of democratic legitimacy. Grimaud illustrates how a general forest-protection policy can support detailed use regulations while leaving punishment to Congress.

The editors caution that describing Congress as principal and the agency as agent simplifies a more complicated relationship: agencies can develop initiatives and seek legislative support, while Congress can enact highly specific requirements or broader delegations under different political conditions. More administrative discretion does not necessarily mean more regulation. Statutory authorization, the validity of the delegation, and the legality of a particular exercise are separate questions.
